- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.5) over recent days, reduce forecasted overshoots; model tends to overreact to positive sentiment.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) or mixed, allow for sharper downward corrections; model often underestimates downside risk.
- When true price drops sharply after a spike, model overcorrects upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next period.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 periods ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–70 range after 70+ peaks, reduce forecasted highs by 3–5%.
- If sentiment is high but price fails to rise, model overestimates momentum — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is low and price remains stable, model overreacts — reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid false bullish signals.
- When sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 5–10% immediately after sentiment shift.
